papers.title: ReFlow: Replay-Driven Decoupling for Efficient RL Post-Training
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has been a critical paradigm for improving large language model (LLM) reasoning and agentic capabilities, but its efficiency remains a major bottleneck. Existing RL systems commonly rely on asynchronous execution to overlap rollout generation with policy optimization for enhanced efficiency. However, this approach faces inherent limitations: mild policy staleness offers only limited training efficiency gains, whereas aggressive asynchrony can degrade model quality and yields diminishing efficiency gains. The dynamic nature of LLM RL and multi-turn agentic workloads further challenges RL system design, as resource demands shift over time, making static resource allocation and generation strategy inefficient. This paper presents ReFlow, a system-algorithm co-designed RL framework for efficient LLM post-training. Its key insight is that, unlike existing RL frameworks which consume each trajectory only once, experience replay of recent trajectories enables effective sample reuse, thereby amortizing the high cost of rollout generation without incurring excessive policy staleness. To fully exploit this opportunity, ReFlow adopts a decoupled and adaptive architecture with three key designs: a dual replay data cycle supports efficient experience reuse while balancing training throughput and optimization stability; an elastic resource pool enables dynamic resource placement to accommodate evolving RL workloads; an adaptive scheduler coordinates generation strategies and resource allocation to improve resource utilization and boost generation throughput. Experiments across representative single-turn reasoning and multi-turn agentic RL tasks show that ReFlow improves training throughput by up to $2.06\times$ over state-of-the-art synchronous and asynchronous RL systems, while maintaining comparable or better model performance.
papers.abstract_zh: 强化学习（RL）一直是提升大语言模型（LLM）推理与智能体能力的关键范式，但其效率仍是主要瓶颈。现有 RL 系统通常依赖异步执行，将 rollout 生成与策略优化重叠以提升效率。然而，这种方法面临固有局限：轻微的策略陈旧只能带来有限的训练效率提升，而激进的异步会降低模型质量且效率收益递减。LLM RL 与多轮智能体工作负载的动态特性进一步挑战 RL 系统设计，因为资源需求随时间变化，使静态资源分配与生成策略效率低下。本文提出 ReFlow，一个面向高效 LLM 后训练的系统-算法协同设计 RL 框架。其关键洞见在于：与现有 RL 框架仅消费每条轨迹一次不同，对近期轨迹进行经验回放可实现有效的样本复用，从而在不引入过度策略陈旧的情况下摊销 rollout 生成的高昂成本。为充分利用这一机会，ReFlow 采用解耦且自适应的架构，包含三项关键设计：双回放数据循环支持高效经验复用，同时平衡训练吞吐与优化稳定性；弹性资源池支持动态资源放置以适应不断演变的 RL 工作负载；自适应调度器协调生成策略与资源分配，以提升资源利用率并提高生成吞吐。在代表性单轮推理与多轮智能体 RL 任务上的实验表明，ReFlow 相比最先进的同步与异步 RL 系统将训练吞吐提升最高达 2.06 倍，同时保持相当或更好的模型性能。
papers.tldr_zh: ReFlow 通过近期轨迹的经验回放实现样本复用，并采用双回放数据循环、弹性资源池与自适应调度器，在单轮推理和多轮智能体 RL 任务上把训练吞吐最高提升 2.06 倍且性能不降。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones
papers.abstract_en: Recent work shows that depth recurrence can be retrofitted into pretrained language models. In this work, we adapt this paradigm for visual understanding, using depth recurrence to reduce the parameter footprint of a pretrained vision-language model (VLM). To this end, we prune layers from the language backbone of the VLM and loop over a subset of the remaining layers. At each step of the loop, a linear adapter merges the block's output with the token representations from the preceding layers and projects the fused representation back into the block. As the pruning impacts the original model performance, we propose a three-stage recovery training: first, we leverage a language-only pretraining to recover the performance of the language backbone, followed by an alignment of the vision-language projector, and a full fine-tuning of the model via visual instruction tuning. In the first and the last stage, we distill the outputs of the pretrained non-recurrent model into the recurrent model, which further improves the recovery. We evaluate the proposed approach on the TinyLLaVA-1.4B backbone without introducing any new vision-language data during retrofitting. Our experiments demonstrate that the retrofitted recurrent model outperforms the unpruned baseline trained with the same recovery data while storing 23.3% fewer language parameters. We further show that the proposed retrofitting recurrence outperforms the setup of converting a recurrent LM into a VLM on the same data. Additionally, our ablations show how design choices, such as the adapter between recurrences and a larger recurrent block, lead to the improved performance of our approach. Finally, we find that our proposed model gains on reasoning-oriented benchmarks, whereas its performance on basic visual understanding benchmarks remains on par with the baseline.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期工作表明，深度循环可以加装到预训练语言模型中。在本工作中，我们将这一范式适配到视觉理解，利用深度循环来减少预训练视觉-语言模型（VLM）的参数占用。为此，我们从 VLM 的语言主干中剪枝层，并对剩余层的子集进行循环。在循环的每一步，一个线性适配器将该块的输出与前序层的 token 表示合并，并将融合后的表示投影回该块。由于剪枝会影响原始模型性能，我们提出三阶段恢复训练：首先利用纯语言预训练恢复语言主干性能，随后对齐视觉-语言投影器，最后通过视觉指令微调对模型进行全量微调。在第一和最后阶段，我们将预训练非循环模型的输出蒸馏到循环模型中，进一步改善恢复效果。我们在 TinyLLaVA-1.4B 主干上评估所提方法，且在加装循环过程中不引入任何新的视觉-语言数据。实验表明，加装循环后的模型优于用相同恢复数据训练的未剪枝基线，同时语言参数存储减少 23.3%。我们进一步表明，所提加装循环方法优于在相同数据上将循环 LM 转换为 VLM 的设置。此外，我们的消融实验显示，循环之间的适配器以及更大的循环块等设计选择如何带来性能提升。最后，我们发现所提模型在面向推理的基准上有所增益，而在基础视觉理解基准上的性能与基线持平。
papers.tldr_zh: 该工作将深度循环加装到预训练 VLM 的语言主干中，通过剪枝并循环部分层、配合三阶段恢复训练与蒸馏，在 TinyLLaVA-1.4B 上以少 23.3% 语言参数超过未剪枝基线，并在推理基准上取得增益。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining, instruction tuning
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）正从辅助科学研究与工程扩展到自主开发与改进 AI 系统，推动 AI for AI（AI4AI）作为通向递归自我改进（RSI）的路径。工作流驱动的机器学习工程（MLE）系统通过管理长时程实验的复杂编排，为这一追求提供了可行路径，而近期 MLE 系统采用模型主导的交互，使模型能够自主组织实验并基于执行反馈调整优化策略。然而，每个实验的反馈反映的是若干先前决策，而一次长 MLE 运行包含许多此类高成本实验。因此训练必须从长交互轨迹中选择有用的监督信号，并从中间结果中学习。我们提出一种面向自主长时程 MLE 优化的后训练方法，并将其用于训练 MLExpert，一个 35B 混合专家智能体模型。我们设计 Kaggle-MLE Factory 来构建可执行任务以及用于模型主导实验的交互框架。分层智能体 SFT 通过结果引导的监督将通用工具使用与编码能力迁移到 MLE。窗口化交互 RL（WIRL）将相邻实验结果之间的多轮决策视为一个执行窗口，并为其分配共享的基于结果的奖励。异步收集与策略校正支持在轨迹结束前进行策略更新。在 MLE-Bench Lite 上，MLExpert 将基础模型的平均奖牌率从 37.9% 提升至 72.7%，达到与 Kimi-K3、GLM-5.3 等更大前沿模型相当的性能。进一步实验表明，MLExpert 在 NatureBench Lite、智能体脚手架优化与算法优化上均有提升，表明所学优化能力可泛化到其他任务。
papers.tldr_zh: 该工作提出面向长时程 MLE 的后训练方法并训练 35B 混合专家模型 MLExpert，采用分层智能体 SFT 与窗口化交互 RL，在 MLE-Bench Lite 上将平均奖牌率从 37.9% 提升至 72.7%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
evidence: 明确的方法贡献：we propose, algorithm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
papers.abstract_en: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.
papers.abstract_zh: 3D 物体组合对数字内容创作和机器人仿真至关重要，同时也是检验基础模型物理智能的关键试验平台。以往方法要么利用大语言模型直接预测物体坐标，要么利用生成式扩散先验合成组合图像以进行视觉对齐，二者都依赖数字空间中的静态先验。然而，这些方法在诸如精确悬挂、重力驱动的沉降和隐藏容纳等复杂组合任务上始终表现不佳，因为这些任务需要涉及全局规划、细粒度对齐和物理仿真的交互式构建过程。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 PhySGA，一个通过智能体探索和物理仿真进行 3D 组合的物理空间接地智能体框架，能够实现刚性、铰接和可变形物体的通用交互式装配。将原始 LLM 或 VLM 直接应用于该任务被证明是不够的，因为当前模型本身缺乏接地的物理理解和交互式构建经验。为克服这一局限，我们设计了一种协同的前馈-反馈架构：装配智能体专注于几何与运动学推理，以进行全局步骤规划和粗调；评判智能体则对接触动力学进行推理，以进行仿真器状态诊断和细粒度闭环校正。此外，动作路由器将语义规划和分析映射为仿真器中可执行的物理原语，而任务特定的自进化技能库将历史试错反馈提炼为可复用经验，从而提高成功率并减少探索尝试次数。在 Isaac Sim 中的大量实验表明，PhySGA 在关系保真度、物理合理性和视觉质量方面显著超越现有方法。
papers.tldr_zh: PhySGA 提出物理空间接地的智能体框架，通过装配智能体与评判智能体协同、动作路由器和自进化技能库，在 Isaac Sim 中实现刚性、铰接与可变形物体的交互式 3D 组合，并在关系保真度、物理合理性和视觉质量上超越现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, foundation model
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.abstract_en: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
papers.abstract_zh: 长上下文大语言模型中注意力机制的设计面临 KV 缓存大小、训练与预填充 FLOPs 以及模型质量之间的“不可能三角”。GQA 取得了良好的质量，但带来较高的 KV 缓存开销；MLA 和 MFA 等替代方法可以压缩缓存，但 MLA 存在质量损失，而 MFA 大幅增加训练和预填充计算量。我们提出虚拟头注意力（VHA），它通过两个轻量线性操作同时改善这三个顶点：Q Premix 对每个 KV 组内的查询施加近似恒等变换，从减半的物理查询头中恢复虚拟头多样性；Linear Postmix 通过低秩的 $I + AB^\top$ 残差结构融合头间特征。由于 VHA 不引入非线性操作，推理时 Premix 可以折叠进查询投影，Postmix 可以折叠进输出投影，使模型退化为标准 GQA-2 架构，从而直接复用所有现有的 GQA 推理优化。仅使用两个 KV 头时，大模型中的组大小很容易达到 64，在解码期间充分利用 Tensor Core 并行性。在 4K 上下文、500 亿 token 预训练的四个规模上，VHA 在每个规模上都持续超越标准 GQA 基线（+0.05% 至 +0.81%），同时在稠密规模上将 KV 缓存相比 GQA-8 减少 4 倍、在 MoE 规模上相比 GQA-4 减少 2 倍，并将训练和预填充 FLOPs 降低 7.9%（1.7B，$S{=}4096$）。在一个以 8K 上下文、5000 亿 token 训练的工业级 30B-A3B MoE 模型上，VHA 在 12 项基准的基础模型评估套件上分别超越 MLA 和 GQA-4 达 +0.70% 和 +2.60%；在另一项匹配的 10B-A1B MoE 长上下文中期训练对比中，VHA 在 8K–128K 上取得平均 RULER 分数 84.4，而 GQA 为 73.0，同时在全注意力层中使用两个而非四个 KV 头。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出虚拟头注意力 VHA，通过 Q Premix 与低秩 Linear Postmix 两个可折叠线性操作，在减少 KV 缓存与训练/预填充 FLOPs 的同时提升质量，四个规模预训练均超越 GQA 基线，并在 30B-A3B MoE 上优于 MLA 和 GQA-4。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
匹配 模型架构：attention mechanism
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DriveWLA: Unifying Future Dynamics and Scene Semantics through World-Language-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and world models have demonstrated strong capabilities in semantic understanding and future scene evolution for autonomous driving. However, effectively integrating both capabilities for trajectory generation remains challenging. In this work, we propose DriveWLA, a unified World-Language-Action model based on Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) that jointly models semantic understanding, future scene dynamics, and trajectory generation. DriveWLA consists of three experts: a World Expert for future prediction, a Language Expert for semantic understanding, and an Action Expert for trajectory generation. We further introduce Cross-Expert Attention, which enables controlled information flow across experts while aligning semantic and dynamic representations. To improve trajectory generation beyond imitation learning, we apply Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning post-training to refine the Action Expert. Extensive experiments show that DriveWLA achieves superior performance in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluation. DriveWLA achieves 92.3 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, demonstrating strong performance among VLM-based and world-model-based planners. Without specific fine-tuning, DriveWLA further demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to HUGSIM, nuScenes, and Bench2Drive. These results validate the effectiveness of our unified World-Language-Action modeling, establishing DriveWLA as a generalizable framework for autonomous driving.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）和世界模型在自动驾驶的语义理解和未来场景演化方面已展现出强大能力。然而，有效整合这两种能力以生成轨迹仍然具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们提出 DriveWLA，一个基于 Transformer 混合（MoT）的统一世界-语言-动作模型，联合建模语义理解、未来场景动态和轨迹生成。DriveWLA 由三个专家组成：用于未来预测的世界专家、用于语义理解的语言专家和用于轨迹生成的动作专家。我们进一步引入跨专家注意力，它在对齐语义和动态表示的同时实现跨专家的受控信息流。为了超越模仿学习改进轨迹生成，我们应用 Flow-GRPO 强化学习后训练来精炼动作专家。大量实验表明，DriveWLA 在开环和闭环评估中均取得优越性能。DriveWLA 在 NAVSIM v1 上达到 92.3 PDMS，在 NAVSIM v2 上达到 90.1 EPDMS，在基于 VLM 和基于世界模型的规划器中展现出强劲性能。无需特定微调，DriveWLA 进一步展现出对 HUGSIM、nuScenes 和 Bench2Drive 的强大零样本泛化能力。这些结果验证了我们统一世界-语言-动作建模的有效性，确立了 DriveWLA 作为自动驾驶可泛化框架的地位。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 Transformer 混合的统一世界-语言-动作模型 DriveWLA，通过世界、语言、动作三个专家与跨专家注意力联合建模，并用 Flow-GRPO 后训练精炼动作专家，在 NAVSIM v1/v2 上分别达到 92.3 PDMS 和 90.1 EPDMS，并零样本泛化到 HUGSIM、nuScenes 和 Bench2Drive。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. We introduce DocPilot, an agentic document framework that supports expressive orchestration and makes complex document solving learnable by small language models (SLMs). DocPilot orchestrates evidence seeking through page-level navigation and fine-grained evidence localization, and integrates local visual inspection, code-based numerical reasoning, and cross-modal reasoning for multimodal understanding. To transfer these capabilities to small models, we propose curriculum-based agentic training that progresses from single-ability learning to adaptive orchestration through supervision from data-grounded reasoning traces and executable interaction trajectories. Across MMLongBench-Doc, DocBench, FinRAGBench-V, and MADQA, DocPilot achieves strong gains with frontier VLM backbones, while DocPilot-4B delivers competitive performance against substantially larger models, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization across diverse long-document reasoning settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态长文档问答要求模型跨页面与模态寻找稀疏证据、理解异构文档内容，并对收集到的证据进行推理。即便是先进的视觉-语言模型（VLM）也可能忽略稀疏证据，并在单次处理中难以进行跨模态推理。现有文档智能体进一步引入多步交互，但其中一些仍依赖预定义工作流或粗粒度动作，限制了文档推理的灵活性与粒度。我们提出 DocPilot，一个智能体文档框架，支持富有表现力的编排，并使复杂文档求解可被小语言模型（SLM）学习。DocPilot 通过页面级导航与细粒度证据定位来编排证据寻找，并整合局部视觉检查、基于代码的数值推理与跨模态推理以实现多模态理解。为将这些能力迁移到小模型，我们提出基于课程的智能体训练，通过来自数据接地的推理轨迹与可执行交互轨迹的监督，从单一能力学习逐步推进到自适应编排。在 MMLongBench-Doc、DocBench、FinRAGBench-V 与 MADQA 上，DocPilot 在前沿 VLM 主干上取得显著增益，而 DocPilot-4B 相比大得多的模型也展现出有竞争力的性能，表明其在多样长文档推理场景中具有强有效性与泛化能力。代码见 https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot。
papers.tldr_zh: DocPilot 通过页面级导航与细粒度证据定位编排文档推理，并用课程式智能体训练将能力迁移到小模型，在多个长文档基准上取得增益，DocPilot-4B 性能可媲美更大模型。

papers.title: CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet real-world applications often require them to continually acquire new capabilities from sequential tasks, i.e., Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). In typical MLLMs, a projector is employed to align visual representations with the language model. However, existing methods primarily protect the language model from forgetting while continuously updating the projector across tasks. Such asymmetric adaptation can cause substantial representation drift in the projector, increasing the mismatch between the projector and language model and consequently exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To address this issue, we propose Compatible Routing (CART), which explicitly coordinates the adaptation of the projector and language model. Specifically, CART maintains task-specific experts for both modules and combines them through weighted mixtures. CART jointly infers their weights by considering both expert relevance and cross-module compatibility, thereby promoting coordinated adaptation between the two modules. To further control model growth, we introduce relevance-guided expert consolidation, which merges experts exhibiting similar relevance profiles across samples within each module. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CART achieves state-of-the-art performance.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）通过指令微调取得强劲性能，但现实应用常要求它们从顺序任务中持续获取新能力，即多模态持续指令微调（MCIT）。在典型 MLLM 中，投影器用于将视觉表示与语言模型对齐。然而，现有方法主要在跨任务持续更新投影器的同时保护语言模型免于遗忘。这种非对称适应会导致投影器出现显著表示漂移，加剧投影器与语言模型之间的不匹配，从而加重灾难性遗忘。为解决该问题，我们提出兼容路由（CART），显式协调投影器与语言模型的适应。具体而言，CART 为两个模块分别维护任务特定专家，并通过加权混合将其组合。CART 通过同时考虑专家相关性与跨模块兼容性来联合推断其权重，从而促进两个模块之间的协调适应。为进一步控制模型增长，我们引入相关性引导的专家合并，在每个模块内合并跨样本具有相似相关性画像的专家。大量实验表明 CART 达到最先进性能。
papers.tldr_zh: CART 为投影器与语言模型分别维护任务特定专家并加权混合，通过联合考虑专家相关性与跨模块兼容性协调两者适应，并合并相似专家，在多模态持续指令微调中达到最先进性能。

papers.title: VELD-QA: A Large-Scale Dataset for Visual Evidence Grounding and Question Answering in Long Documents
papers.abstract_en: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. We present VELD-QA, a large-scale benchmark for Visual Evidence grounding and question answering in Long Documents. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. We evaluate nine vision-language models under four evidence settings and seven retrieval-augmented and agentic systems. Our analysis identifies bottlenecks in evidence localization and interpretation. Retrieval-based methods substantially underperform the oracle setting with ground-truth supporting pages; full-document access does not close the gap. Localization alone is insufficient: oracle accuracy peaks at 81.7%, highlighting persistent visual interpretation and reasoning challenges. Enriching inputs with our visual-element annotations narrows the performance gap by 17-24%, demonstrating value beyond evaluation and motivating data enrichment for multimodal document QA. Our code is available at https://github.com/oracle-samples/veld-qa.

papers.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.
papers.abstract_zh: 实现通用空间智能需要统一理解静态 3D 和动态 4D。然而，我们发现现有模型难以同时在这两方面表现出色：3D 后训练会削弱动态理解，而 4D 专用模型往往缺乏强大的静态 3D 推理能力。我们的分析表明，这种空间-动态干扰在参数组之间高度不均匀，静态与动态能力之间的平衡对后层 MLP 的变化尤为敏感。为解决这种干扰，我们提出 DynThinker，一个联合增强静态与动态空间推理的统一框架。解耦指数移动平均（D-EMA）应用可配置的分组平均，以约束对干扰敏感的预训练参数的漂移，同时保留能力增强的灵活性。空间-动态融合（SDF）通过语义引导，选择性地将动态几何编码器中的空间和时间先验整合到 VLM 中间表示中，从而与 D-EMA 互补。在涵盖九个静态 3D 和动态 4D 基准的十项指标上，DynThinker 在所有评估模型中取得最高平均分。值得注意的是，DynThinker 在 ReVSI 上达到 56.0，在 DSR-Bench 上达到 67.2，在 DSI-Bench 的逐样本和逐组评估协议下分别达到 51.2 和 40.1，在统一模型中于全部四项评估上创下所比较开源模型中的新最先进结果。
papers.tldr_zh: DynThinker 通过解耦指数移动平均（D-EMA）和空间-动态融合（SDF）缓解静态 3D 与动态 4D 推理之间的干扰，在九个基准的十项指标上取得最高平均分，并在 ReVSI、DSR-Bench 和 DSI-Bench 上创下开源模型新最先进结果。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models for tables and relational databases are increasingly used for predictive tasks across various scientific and industrial domains. However, adapting existing models to unseen datasets requires tens of thousands of examples. Here we introduce RT-J, an 86M-parameter relational foundation model (RFM) that makes accurate predictions even with hundreds of in-context examples or fewer. To achieve this, we first assemble the Join, a large collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks. We pretrain with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells, using in-context examples from a novel lightweight random-walk retriever. Finally, we leverage context tuning and ensembling to scale up test-time compute. On in-context regression tasks from RelBench, RT-J requires 10x fewer examples on average to match strong feature engineering pipelines with LLM-agent or RDBLearn featurizers and TabICLv2 or LightGBM predictors. Overall, our work pushes the frontier for context-efficient predictions on relational data and highlights the importance of real-world semantics, context engineering and large-scale pretraining for RFMs.

papers.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
papers.abstract_en: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD), which explicitly detects and penalizes stagnation in student-generated trajectories. ProD encodes the stagnation gap between student and teacher into an adaptive margin for dynamically penalizing possible stagnation. By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior. Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管基于 LLM 的智能体系统在推理和解决复杂现实任务方面表现出卓越能力，但它们也带来大量 token 消耗和推理延迟，限制了实际部署。为提升智能体系统的效率，近期工作致力于通过基于监督微调的蒸馏，将智能体能力从大规模模型迁移到小语言模型（SLM）。然而，随着交互轨迹变长，涉及更长的推理-行动链和大量环境反馈，被蒸馏的学生智能体往往出现进展停滞：陷入以持续失败策略和难以取得有意义进展为特征的低效循环。我们的系统分析表明，这一现象在不同 SLM 和任务领域中一致出现。为解决该问题，我们提出进展感知蒸馏（ProD），它显式检测并惩罚学生生成轨迹中的停滞。ProD 将学生与教师之间的停滞差距编码为自适应间隔，以动态惩罚可能的停滞。通过迭代应用该过程，ProD 使学生智能体逐步逼近教师行为。涉及 8 个 SLM（参数规模从 0.6B 到 8B）、在域内和域外基准上的大量实验表明，ProD 显著缓解进展停滞，同时提升被蒸馏 SLM 智能体的成功率和任务完成效率。
papers.tldr_zh: ProD 通过将学生与教师之间的停滞差距编码为自适应间隔来检测并惩罚学生轨迹中的停滞，在 8 个 0.6B 至 8B 的 SLM 上缓解进展停滞并提升成功率与任务完成效率。

papers.title: ActICL: Post-Training for Agentic Multimodal In-Context Learning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal in-context learning (ICL) is an important capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Its performance is closely tied to the demonstrations it uses, making demonstration retrieval a core problem for ICL. Common methods use fixed scoring methods to retrieve all the demonstrations at once, which may introduce redundancy and noise. Context-aware retrieval methods have emerged to address this problem by allowing incremental retrieval from a growing context. However, none of them lets the MLLM learn how to judge what new demonstrations it needs and then carry out progressive retrieval on its own. To this end, we introduce ActICL, which trains an MLLM agent to acquire and use an ICL context via tool-augmented reasoning. An ActICL agent analyzes its own information gaps during iterative reasoning and tool-use actions. Based on these gaps, it performs targeted retrieval to acquire a set of initial candidates. It can then use the existing context to further filter the candidates and refine the context, or it can iteratively perform a new retrieval. When the agent judges that the context is sufficient for the task, or when the resource limit is reached with the user request met, it sends the acquired context to an answering model, either the agent itself or another MLLM. We use a two-stage post-training procedure that jointly optimizes the agent's acquisition and answering. With an adaptive number of demonstrations, ActICL improves average performance by 11.6 percentage points over standard similarity-based retrieval across seven benchmarks and three MLLMs, and by 4.4 points compared to the strongest prior baseline. The contexts acquired by ActICL agents can also be used effectively by frontier models. When GPT-5.6-Sol performs 4-shot ICL, ActICL's contexts improve its performance by 3.5 points over standard retrieval, averaged over three benchmarks.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态上下文学习（ICL）是多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的一项重要能力。其性能与所使用的示例密切相关，使示例检索成为 ICL 的核心问题。常见方法使用固定评分方法一次性检索所有示例，这可能引入冗余和噪声。上下文感知检索方法通过允许从不断增长的上下文中增量检索来应对该问题。然而，这些方法都没有让 MLLM 学会判断自己需要哪些新示例，并自行进行渐进式检索。为此，我们提出 ActICL，它训练一个 MLLM 智能体通过工具增强推理来获取并使用 ICL 上下文。ActICL 智能体在迭代推理和工具使用动作中分析自身的信息缺口。基于这些缺口，它执行针对性检索以获取一组初始候选。随后它可利用现有上下文进一步过滤候选并精炼上下文，或迭代执行新的检索。当智能体判断上下文足以完成任务，或在满足用户请求的前提下达到资源限制时，它将获取的上下文发送给回答模型，该模型可以是智能体自身或另一个 MLLM。我们采用两阶段后训练流程，联合优化智能体的获取与回答。在自适应数量的示例下，ActICL 在七个基准和三个 MLLM 上相较标准相似度检索平均提升 11.6 个百分点，相较最强先前基线提升 4.4 个百分点。ActICL 智能体获取的上下文也可被前沿模型有效使用。当 GPT-5.6-Sol 执行 4-shot ICL 时，ActICL 的上下文在三个基准上平均相较标准检索提升其性能 3.5 个百分点。
papers.tldr_zh: ActICL 通过两阶段后训练让 MLLM 智能体在工具增强推理中分析信息缺口并渐进式检索、过滤和精炼 ICL 上下文，在七个基准和三个 MLLM 上平均超越标准相似度检索 11.6 个百分点。

papers.title: Beyond Static Positional Encoding: Bayesian Time-aware Attention for Non-Stationary Long-term Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: Transformers have demonstrated strong performance in long-term time series forecasting (LTSF), yet modeling non-stationary temporal dependencies remains challenging. In this paper, we interpret self-attention as a Bayesian posterior over attended positions, combining a content-based prior induced by scaled dot-product similarity with a temporal-evidence likelihood induced by positional encoding. This formulation provides a probabilistic interpretation of how positional encoding shapes the temporal dependencies captured by self-attention. Building on this perspective, we derive a population-level evidence lower bound (ELBO) that characterizes the role of positional encoding in forecasting weakly stationary time series. Our analysis further highlights a limitation of static positional encoding: when temporal dependence structures vary across input windows, a fixed temporal bias must accommodate heterogeneous dynamics and can therefore be suboptimal for non-stationary forecasting. Motivated by this analysis, we propose Bayesian Time-aware Attention (BTA), which employs a mixture-of-experts (MoE) router to adaptively combine temporal kernels and generate input-conditioned, head-specific positional biases. Extensive experiments on standard LTSF benchmarks demonstrate that BTA consistently improves forecasting performance across multiple Transformer backbones and achieves competitive overall performance with modest computational overhead and stable training.
papers.abstract_zh: Transformer 在长期时间序列预测（LTSF）中表现出强大性能，但建模非平稳时间依赖仍然具有挑战性。本文将自注意力解释为对被关注位置的贝叶斯后验，结合由缩放点积相似度诱导的基于内容的先验与由位置编码诱导的时间证据似然。这一形式化为位置编码如何塑造自注意力所捕获的时间依赖提供了概率解释。基于此视角，我们推导出一个群体级证据下界（ELBO），刻画位置编码在预测弱平稳时间序列中的作用。我们的分析进一步凸显了静态位置编码的局限：当时间依赖结构在不同输入窗口间变化时，固定的时间偏置必须适应异质动态，因而对非平稳预测可能次优。受此分析启发，我们提出贝叶斯时间感知注意力（BTA），它使用混合专家（MoE）路由器自适应地组合时间核，并生成以输入为条件、特定于注意力头的位置偏置。在标准 LTSF 基准上的大量实验表明，BTA 在多个 Transformer 骨干上持续提升预测性能，并以适度的计算开销和稳定的训练取得有竞争力的整体性能。
papers.tldr_zh: 将自注意力解释为贝叶斯后验并推导 ELBO，提出用 MoE 路由器生成输入条件化位置偏置的 BTA，在多个 Transformer 骨干上提升长期时间序列预测性能。

papers.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
papers.abstract_en: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines. Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex. Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents' robustness to noise while maintaining stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型已从单轮聊天机器人演变为能够进行长时程推理的交互式智能体。在实际部署中，MCP 工具服务可能返回带噪声的反馈，用户也可能介入纠正智能体，但现有方法对反思学习与失败恢复提供的监督有限。为弥补这一差距，我们提出 Agent-Reflex，一个用于激励智能体主动反思的通用训练框架。具体而言，Agent-Reflex 包含三个阶段。首先，环境反思技能发现（RSD）在环境扩展中注入有依据的工具反馈扰动，采样能力多样的 LLM 池，挖掘匹配的成功-失败对，并总结可复用的反思元技能。在此技能库基础上，我们应用反思监督微调（ReSFT），将每项技能转化为对自我反思、技能恢复和以用户为中心的纠正的监督，强化互补的反思行为。最后，我们提出同策略反思策略优化（ORPO），将噪声交互下的智能体强化学习与反思引导的同策略蒸馏相结合，以进一步激发主动反思。基于 Qwen3-8B，Agent-Reflex 在五个长时程工具使用基准上达到 58.6 的总体成绩，在 AgentNoiseBench 上达到 29.1，超越了强大的环境扩展与反思基线。在六个具有挑战性的智能体基准套件上的实验证明了 Agent-Reflex 的有效性。进一步分析表明，Agent-Reflex 提升了智能体对噪声的鲁棒性，同时保持稳定的训练动态，支持可扩展的智能体训练。我们的代码见 https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex。
papers.tldr_zh: Agent-Reflex 通过环境反思技能发现、反思监督微调和同策略反思策略优化三阶段训练框架，激励语言智能体主动反思，在长时程工具使用与噪声交互基准上超越环境扩展和反思基线。

papers.title: MicroCLIP: Connecting Text and Microscopy Images via Contrastive Language--Image Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Understanding fluorescence microscopy images is fundamental to automating biological research. However, existing methods typically learn predefined concepts from closed-set data, limiting transfer across tasks and biological contexts. In this work, we introduce MicroCLIP, a vision-language model that learns generalizable cellular and subcellular representations from natural language supervision for open-set image classification and retrieval. To pretrain MicroCLIP, we construct MicroPool-2M, a dataset of approximately 2.5 million fluorescence microscopy image-text pairs spanning diverse cellular structures, cell lines, and imaging conditions. Aligning microscopy images with biological concepts in natural language is challenging because most images lack descriptive captions and biological knowledge annotations. We therefore progressively establish image-text associations at three levels to provide MicroCLIP with richer semantic supervision: (1) category-level alignment links images to standardized labels defined by subcellular structure-cell-line combinations; (2) knowledge-level alignment incorporates biological priors derived from these labels to capture relationships across species and cell types; and (3) detail-level alignment uses a multimodal large language model to recaption and verify image-text pairs at scale, emphasizing fine-grained visual characteristics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MicroCLIP achieves leading performance in zero-shot classification and text-image retrieval on microscopy images. It retrieves images with specific cellular characteristics from thousands of candidates and generalizes to unseen biological concepts without additional supervision. These results highlight MicroCLIP's potential as a foundation model for fluorescence microscopy.
papers.abstract_zh: 理解荧光显微图像是自动化生物学研究的基础。然而，现有方法通常从闭集数据中学习预定义概念，限制了跨任务和跨生物语境的迁移。在本工作中，我们提出 MicroCLIP，一个视觉-语言模型，从自然语言监督中学习可泛化的细胞与亚细胞表征，用于开集图像分类和检索。为预训练 MicroCLIP，我们构建了 MicroPool-2M，一个约 250 万荧光显微图像-文本对的数据集，涵盖多样的细胞结构、细胞系和成像条件。将显微图像与自然语言中的生物学概念对齐具有挑战性，因为大多数图像缺乏描述性标题和生物学知识标注。因此，我们在三个层次上逐步建立图像-文本关联，为 MicroCLIP 提供更丰富的语义监督：（1）类别级对齐将图像链接到由亚细胞结构-细胞系组合定义的标准化标签；（2）知识级对齐引入由这些标签导出的生物学先验，以捕捉跨物种和细胞类型的关系；（3）细节级对齐使用多模态大语言模型大规模重写标题并验证图像-文本对，强调细粒度视觉特征。大量实验表明，MicroCLIP 在显微图像的零样本分类和文本-图像检索上取得领先性能。它能够从数千个候选中检索具有特定细胞特征的图像，并在无额外监督的情况下泛化到未见过的生物学概念。这些结果凸显了 MicroCLIP 作为荧光显微基础模型的潜力。
papers.tldr_zh: MicroCLIP 构建约 250 万图像-文本对的 MicroPool-2M 数据集，通过类别级、知识级和细节级三层对齐进行对比语言-图像预训练，在荧光显微图像的零样本分类与检索上取得领先性能。

papers.title: Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation
papers.abstract_en: A language model can generate several solutions to the same problem, some leading to correct answers and others to incorrect ones. Many post-training methods turn these trajectories into learning signals using supervision from reference answers, verifiable feedback, or external teachers. Without such supervision, learning from the model's own generations becomes less straightforward, as their correctness cannot be reliably assessed. An incorrect solution may nevertheless contain useful intermediate reasoning, so its value as supervision need not be determined solely by its final answer. Can a model improve by learning from its unverified peer solutions without first determining which are correct? We propose Shared Residual Distillation (SRD), an on-policy self-distillation method that learns from the model's own unverified peer trajectories. SRD compares how peers change the prediction distribution relative to a control, retaining adjustments that agree in direction and are conservative in magnitude. This yields supervision without treating any complete solution as correct, and the trained model requires no peers at inference time. Starting from the corresponding base models, SRD raises mean AIME24--26 avg@12 from 11.02 to 16.20 on Qwen3-1.7B, from 19.07 to 45.46 on Qwen3-4B, and from 21.39 to 54.44 on Qwen3-8B. Controlled ablations support the value of the shared-residual construction, and we observe no degradation relative to the base models on two general-capability benchmarks.

papers.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
papers.abstract_en: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

papers.title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Improving the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) often relies on post-training with supervision from stronger models. Two common strategies are supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which trains on teacher-generated demonstrations, and on-policy distillation (OPD), which provides teacher feedback on trajectories generated by the student itself. While OPD can be more data-efficient by supervising student-generated trajectories, it is unclear how the teacher's supervision at each state affects the student's learned behavior. To study this question, we conduct a controlled comparison of OPD and filtered SFT across data budgets and tasks where the teacher exhibits different levels of reliability, and analyze how these differences shape student accuracy and completion behavior. Across the two tasks, we find that OPD is effective only when the teacher remains reliable on student-generated trajectories. On ChartQA, where the teacher completes 99% of its solutions, OPD trained on only 10% of the data comes within 1.4 accuracy points of full-data SFT. In contrast, on Geometry3K, where the teacher fails to complete 22% of its solutions, OPD underperforms SFT by 7.9 points, with most of the gap explained by incomplete responses. More strikingly, starting OPD from an SFT student reduces its completion rate from 76% to 62%, effectively erasing the completion behavior learned through SFT. Filtering teacher demonstrations for completeness alone recovers much of SFT's advantage. These results show that on-policy supervision can transfer not only teacher knowledge but also persistent failure modes on student-visited states. Code is available at https://github.com/ffy208/opd-inherits-teacher-vlm.

papers.title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在空间推理方面取得了实质性进展，自进化智能体通过从交互中学习进一步将这些能力扩展到具身环境。然而，当前的自进化在具身空间任务中仍然特别具有挑战性，基于部分视觉证据的复杂多步决策使得难以确定执行失败的原因。失败可能源于感知错误、探索不足或规划错误，但仅凭执行反馈很少能揭示哪个组件应负责。因此，简单累积交互经验可能强化无效策略。为解决这一问题，我们提出 HiMeco，一种受大脑启发的具身空间智能自进化智能体，其灵感来自元认知监控和海马体记忆巩固。通过海马体-元认知反思，HiMeco 诊断感知-探索-规划（PEP）中的失败，然后比较执行尝试以推导可复用策略和避免重复错误的指导。它还将交互程序抽象为参数化技能，使用证据契约和基于执行的验证来决定其保留与复用。这些策略和技能指导后续交互，记忆仅在轮次之间更新，模型参数保持冻结。HiMeco 在 ESI-Bench 上取得最先进性能，并且在没有进化的情况下也将 EmbSpatial-Bench 上的准确率提升了 3.94 个百分点。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出受元认知与海马体启发的自进化智能体 HiMeco，通过反思诊断感知-探索-规划失败并抽象可复用技能，在 ESI-Bench 上达到最先进并在 EmbSpatial-Bench 上提升 3.94 个百分点。

papers.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
papers.abstract_en: Orthogonal transforms have emerged as an effective tool for low-bit quantization of large language models (LLMs), as they reshape activation distributions without changing the underlying model function. Existing approaches typically rely either on fixed data-agnostic transforms, such as Hadamard rotations, or on calibration-time optimization of learned rotations. We study rotation selection from first principles and show that maximizing covariance leads to spectral alignment and provides a principled criterion for constructing quantization-friendly orthogonal transforms. Based on this insight, we propose SpectrumQuant, a closed-form rotation method that estimates activation covariance from calibration data and uses it to construct a covariance-aware orthogonal transform for post-training quantization. Our formulation characterizes quantization-friendly rotations as compositions of alignment and mixing components, while recovering Hadamard matrices as a special case. Interestingly, a class of butterfly matrices belongs to this category. In the realm of LLM quantization, SpectrumQuant bridges the gap between data-agnostic structured rotations and learned rotations, providing an effective and efficient data-aware alternative for post-training quantization. Experiments on Llama and Mistral models show that SpectrumQuant is competitive with state-of-the-art rotation strategies while requiring less than one-third of the GPU memory and significantly less time than learned rotations approaches like SpinQuant and DartQuant.

papers.title: Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) demand efficient inference, where the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations in linear projections dominate compute and energy cost. Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces this cost by mapping weights and activations to low-bit integers. Power-of-Two (PoT) weight quantization promises efficient multiplier-free LLM inference via shift-add logic, but suffers significant accuracy degradation at low bitwidths due to its coarse base-2 quantization grid. We introduce Fractional PoT (FPoT), a base-$\sqrt{2}$ (half-octave) fractional PoT grid that achieves practical 4-bit weight quantization while preserving a fully integer shift-add datapath. The method combines (i) the base-$\sqrt{2}$ weight grid with uniform integer activations, (ii) a calibration-time grid-alignment refinement absorbed into the static per-channel scale, and (iii) a lightweight 1-adder $\sqrt{2}$ approximation whose error is absorbed during weight calibration via approximate-grid quantization, yielding a processing element (PE) with significantly fewer gates than a 4-bit integer multiplier. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weight and activation quantization, FPoT improves zero-shot commonsense reasoning performance by 8.72% relative to the PoT baseline, while maintaining performance close to the uniform integer baseline, with only a negligible 0.4%p degradation. These results hold across various configurations spanning seven models and three bit-widths. Furthermore, FPoT can be integrated with state-of-the-art LLM PTQ methods, demonstrating framework-agnostic applicability.

papers.title: RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in complex tasks, including code generation, tool use, and multi-hop question answering. Existing self-improvement methods enhance agent performance through model optimization, harness evolution, and executable artifact refinement, while recursive self-improvement (RSI) further extends optimization to the improvement mechanisms themselves. However, adapting self-improvement workflows to evolving performance bottlenecks while improving workflow orchestration through execution feedback remains a key challenge. We propose \textbf{RSIFlow}, a \textbf{R}ecursive \textbf{S}elf-\textbf{I}mprovement framework that integrates adaptive work\textbf{flow} orchestration with meta-agent capability evolution. RSIFlow diagnoses performance bottlenecks from task-agent trajectories and environmental feedback to dynamically select component-specific improvement workflows. The meta-agent then distills workflow outcomes into component-specific skills and cross-component principles, evolving its own harness to improve subsequent workflow orchestration. Experiments across six benchmarks and two backbone models show that RSIFlow achieves the SOTA average performance on all benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate the contributions of adaptive workflow orchestration and meta-harness evolution. Code is available at https://github.com/1HUAN1/RSI-Flow.

papers.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has become a widely adopted approach for aligning vision-language models (VLMs), yet the security of multimodal preference data remains largely unexplored. Existing preference poisoning attacks either corrupt explicit supervision signals or require visible triggers, making them detectable under human inspection. We introduce DPOison-VL, the first clean preference poisoning attack against VLM-DPO, which manipulates model alignment solely through imperceptible perturbations on a small fraction of training images, while leaving all prompts, responses, and preference annotations semantically intact. We formulate poison construction as a bilevel optimization and derive a gradient alignment surrogate that efficiently steers image perturbations toward the attacker-specified preference. We further introduce a preference displacement score for principled poison selection with provable first-order optimality under a fixed poison budget, and derive a sufficient condition for preference inversion. Extensive experiments across diverse attack tasks, different VLM architectures and scales, and baseline comparisons demonstrate that DPOison-VL achieves up to 98\% ASR with only 2\% poisoned data and exhibits cross-model transferability, while largely preserving clean accuracy and general utility. Our findings reveal a critical vulnerability in VLM-DPO, where imperceptible image perturbations in preference training data can silently redirect alignment.

papers.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
papers.abstract_en: LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode. To jointly optimize mode selection and within-mode execution, we develop COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode-Execution Training), which decouples the trajectory-level advantage into separate signals for mode selection and within-mode execution, enabling more targeted credit assignment to each decision level. We further introduce progressive exploration, which gradually shifts training from externally assigned modes to autonomous selection, so that the router first learns how to execute each mode before deciding when to use it. We evaluate RouteWeaver across mathematics, coding, knowledge, logical reasoning, and factual recall. RouteWeaver achieves an average accuracy of 61.4%, an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, and outperforms all compared baselines in each of the five domains. Ablations show that both COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration are important for adaptive routing; without progressive exploration, the routing policy collapses entirely to single-round execution.

papers.title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content-safety red-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems. We propose PROBE (Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration), an algorithm for training LLM-based auditors that interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe them for policy violations through multi-turn, tool-mediated dialogue. We formalize agent auditing as a two-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity. To study training objectives and reward design, we compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization in a controlled setting. Across extensive experiments, auditors trained with PROBE uncover substantially broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor is significantly smaller than the target agent. Our results show that multi-turn behavioral auditing is a distinct and necessary axis of agent evaluation, complementing capability and safety benchmarks. PROBE offers a scalable path toward automated policy auditing for real-world agentic systems and suggests a co-evolutionary loop in which auditors expose failures and agents improve from auditor feedback.

papers.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Visual Representation for Spatial Understanding in MLLMs?
papers.abstract_en: Spatial understanding is a necessary step in moving multimodal large language models (MLLMs) toward reasoning about the 3D physical world. Their visual pretraining data, however, is almost entirely 2D, so the visual tokens processed by MLLMs often lack inherent 3D structural information. A growing number of methods inject such structure by transferring representations from external vision or geometry models, and collectively establish that such transfer helps. Behind these methods lies a largely underexplored question: what makes a visual representation good for spatial understanding? To answer it, we first separate what is transferred from how it is transferred, and then trace the resulting differences back to properties of the representations themselves. What we transfer comes from 3D geometry models, self-supervised image and video models, vision-language models, and generative models, in the form of latent features or explicit depth and point maps. We transfer it either by distillation, using it as a supervision target, or by fusion, feeding it as an additional input. We find that a representation's 3D structure correlates strongly with how much it helps, measured by cross-view consistency for latent features and by depth and reconstruction accuracy for explicit geometry. We further show that the form of a representation dictates the mechanism it needs. Latent features gain as much from fusion as from distillation; explicit geometry gains little from fusion, and most of its distillation gain depends on a geometry decoding head. Guided by these findings, we distill both latent features and explicit geometry into a single MLLM. Taking only RGB video as input, it consistently improves over its base model on both static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
papers.abstract_en: We investigate whether per-layer, per-task-phase (prompt/reasoning/response) expert-routing statistics in a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model can guide layer-wise mixed-precision quantization of routed-expert FFN tensors (down/gate and up). To attain layerwise routing statistics, we build a routing-capture and profiling pipeline for Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B in ik_llama.cpp, derive a composite sensitivity score from routing entropy/decisiveness, coefficient of variation (CV), Jaccard/phase-fragility, and top-1 expert strength, and use coordinate descent to tune a layer allocation that respects a fixed average bits-per-weight budget. Notably, the profiling pipeline is applicable to standard top-k MoE architectures. Across independent experimental conditions (about 4.0 bpw flat, about 2.7 bpw steep, and about 2.7 bpw random allocation as a control), reallocation fails to outperform the uniform baseline within each quality tier. In the flat regime, reallocation is statistically neutral (z about 0.9). For the steep tier, the random reallocation performs within 1 SE of the routing-guided reallocation at the same tier, indicating a structural loss at this quality rung caused by mandatory downgrades and Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) tail injection. This aggressive-budget condition shows a decisive loss (z greater than 4 SE) replicated across three independent weight vectors. We argue that the deeper issue is that routing-behavior statistics are an unvalidated proxy for true per-layer quantization cost.

papers.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, yet their susceptibility to backdoor attacks remains a formidable challenge. While existing defenses have evolved from visual-centric patch cues to unsupervised internal attention statistics, they are fundamentally constrained by a reliance on static snapshots and attack-specific heuristics. Given the intricate interplay between dual modalities, the vast design space for multimodal triggers allows diverse threats, such as textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers, to easily circumvent such rigid priors, particularly when attack types are unknown in real-world applications. In this paper, we rethink backdoor detection by shifting the diagnostic paradigm from static observations to dynamic output evolution. We observe that a successful attack inevitably hijacks the model's decoding trajectory, skewing internal modal contributions during generation while maintaining an abnormal output invariance despite input perturbations. To capture this behavior, we propose EVO-Detect, a unified detection framework that monitors the dynamic evolution of internal signals during early decoding steps through two complementary channels: Attention Flow and Logits Flow. The attention branch measures how image-text attention allocation evolves during early generation, whereas the logits branch quantifies the sensitivity of the output distribution to modal perturbations through interventional ablations. We then convert these trajectories into compact sample-level metrics and normalize them against negative-control signatures so that natural perturbations are less likely to be mistaken for backdoor evidence. Extensive evaluations show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as BYE and TCAP across diverse attack families.

papers.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
papers.abstract_en: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). Our formulation allows pre-trained attention layers to be replaced without training a new language model from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Titan-Llama raises accuracy over segmented attention windows from 23.87\% to 40.51\% on QuALITY and from 14.50\% to 40.75\% on LongHealth. Inference benchmarks show more than 20\% faster prefill, 37\% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24\% lower steady-state decode memory usage in the evaluated configurations. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating memory architecture mechanisms that utilize test-time training effectively modulates long-context behavior of pre-trained models, offering a practical route to adapting pre-trained transformers for efficient long-context inference. Our code is released on Github \href{https://github.com/sarahpannn/titans-pytorch/tree/main}{GitHub}

papers.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
papers.abstract_en: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. We post-train Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it through self-play and evaluate transfer to seven unseen natural-language collaboration tasks. CoSIR achieves the highest aggregate score, while its performance in general tasks remains competitive. Behavioral analyses show increased disclosure of private evidence and fewer judged failures to use teammates' input.

papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
papers.abstract_en: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.

papers.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
papers.abstract_en: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

papers.title: Plan-Bench: Can Existing VLMs Go Well Beyond Perception to Reason and Plan in Embodied Worlds?
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in visual perception and spatial reasoning, leading to growing interest in using them as high-level planners for embodied AI. However, physical tasks require models to integrate spatial information, reason over temporal states, and generate multi-step plans under various constraints, raising the question of whether current VLMs can reliably support such reasoning and planning independently of execution. We introduce Plan-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating the high-level reasoning and multi-step planning capabilities of VLMs relevant to embodied worlds, while isolating the influence of action execution. It covers three complementary dimensions, spanning 16 subclasses and 699 curated samples. Extensive evaluation of 28 VLMs reveals room for improvement, with even the strongest model achieving only 75.0% accuracy. We further find that model scaling generally improves these capabilities. Ablation studies also indicate larger models show increasing potential as high-level planners. Overall, Plan-Bench provides a lightweight probe for evaluating VLMs' reasoning and planning capabilities relevant to embodied environments and assessing their potential as decision makers for physical tasks. Our benchmark and code are available at https://github.com/MinneFeng/Plan-Bench.

papers.title: P2Patch: Exploit-Guided Vulnerability Repair
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents for automated program repair, patching software vulnerabilities through multi-step reasoning and tool use. Yet these systems typically validate a patch against the same evidence used to construct it -- a static alert, sanitizer trace, published exploit, or test suite. A patch that blocks that one piece of evidence can therefore look successful while remaining vulnerable to the same vulnerability with some variation. We present P2Patch, a generative adversarial repair system that treats each patch as a new attack target. Starting from a normalized vulnerability finding, an exploitation agent constructs a reproducing proof of vulnerability (PoV), a patching agent repairs the program, and the exploitation agent then attacks the patched program for a distinct same-vulnerability exploit. Every successful exploit becomes a permanent repair requirement, and the final patch must block all PoVs accumulated during the patching process, with construction-time PoVs kept strictly separate from held-out evaluation oracles. Across 101 C/C++ and Java CVE subjects, this adversarial loop surfaces a distinct confirmed exploit in 41% of runs after the patch has already blocked its original construction-time PoV. Against single-pass repair from the same finding using Claude Code, P2Patch raises held-out fix-closed coverage from 78.1% to 84.7% and beyond-upstream coverage from 42.1% to 62.5%. Under the same held-out oracles, it also certifies more attack paths as blocked than recent state-of-the-art agentic repair systems on overlapping subjects. These results show that adversarial testing and independent security oracles expose repair gaps that one-shot validation misses.

papers.title: Frustratingly Easy Majority Voting Using Length Conditioning
papers.abstract_en: Majority Voting (MV) is a simple and widely used strategy which improves the reasoning accuracy of Large Language Models (LLMs) by allocating additional inference-time computation. Specifically, in MV multiple Chain-of-Thoughts (CoTs) are independently sampled and the most frequent final answer is selected. In this work, we propose Length-Conditioned Majority Voting (LCMV), a Test-Time Training approach which improves MV leveraging an empirical observation that has recently been established in several studies: longer CoTs tend to be associated with a lower probability of correctness. We formulate this inductive bias as a length-conditioned prior probability, which is modeled by a simple logistic function. Moreover, we adapt this prior at test time using only unlabeled testing data and without fine-tuning the LLM. Finally, the adapted prior is used to weight the vote of each sampled answer. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and reasoning benchmarks show that LCMV consistently improves over both standard MV and existing length-based and confidence-based aggregation strategies, while retaining the simplicity and model-agnostic nature of MV. Our code is available at: https://github.com/aimagelab/LCMV.

papers.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
papers.abstract_en: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show. Video World Models (VWMs) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task-relevant visual content as additional evidence. However, existing approaches typically invoke a VWM through fixed pipelines centered on a predefined form of visual imagination, such as novel-view synthesis. To support flexible visual imagination for diverse reasoning tasks, we introduce CoWorld Reasoner, an agentic framework that uses a VWM as a unified visual reasoning engine. Its Video World Model-Driven Harness exposes multiple visual operations through tools and uses skills to guide the VLM in deciding whether to imagine, selecting an operation, constructing a generation request, and interpreting the resulting visual evidence. We further introduce VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution, which jointly revises tools, skills, and execution code based on execution feedback while keeping both model weights fixed. Across seven benchmarks spanning spatial intelligence, temporal and causal reasoning, and perceptual reasoning, CoWorld Reasoner outperforms direct reasoning with the same VLM. The strongest variant improves on all seven benchmarks, including relative accuracy gains of 11.8% on MMSI and 13.0% on ERQA, and outperforms all five evolving baselines using the same backbone across five benchmarks.

papers.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
papers.abstract_en: Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. Built on a dual-axis Transformer architecture, OrionMoE-Small selectively activates experts along the feature axis, with routing decisions informed by both individual feature representations and the broader dataset context. This design enables adaptive allocation of computation across heterogeneous tabular problems while retaining a shared computational pathway across tasks. OrionMoE-Small is pretrained entirely on synthetic classification tasks generated from a structured causal prior and performs downstream prediction without gradient-based adaptation. Experiments across multiple tabular benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance against substantially larger foundation models, with particularly strong results on small-context and high-dimensional datasets. Further analysis reveals favorable relative performance under class imbalance and highlights the importance of feature composition.

papers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
papers.abstract_en: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VideoHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VideoHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.
